text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Respected merchant bank Rothschild Australia said 98 per cent of Optus Vision is worth A$1.6 billion, however, equally well-respected accountants Coopers & Lybrand believe it is only worth A$3. The disparity in estimates stems from Kerry Stokes' claim that the Seven Network has the right to buy 98 per cent of Optus Vision. Page 1.

Australian Wheat Board spokesman Alec Nichol confirmed yesterday the AWB has made a 110,000-tonne sale to Egypt, bringing the total amount sold to Egypt so far this season to 340,000 tonnes. The latest contract keeps the AWB on track to export a record voume of wheat in the first quarter this year. Page 2.

The Howard Cabinet is looking at ways it can reduce the A$150 million or more in merchant and broker fees in relation to the part-sale of Telstra. There is a strong interest in the Telstra sale from the broking community, with 140 finance representativesattending an initial briefing this month. Cabinet has not decided whether it will accept underwriting risk for the Telstra float, yet this is highly likely. Page 3.

Grant Samuel's Ross Grant said yesterday the operators of both the casino and the hotel at Reef Casino Trust Ltd are willing to give up their tenure in order to find a solution to the casino's financial troubles. While neither Touraust's Country Comfort or Casinos Austria International Ltd wishes to give up their leases, they would to ensure an injection of capital. Page 19.

The chances of a merger between Crown Casino and Sydney Harbour Casino looked better yesterday as Crown announced it had begun talks with Hudson Conway Ltd to buy the management rights for the A$1.7 billion Melbourne casino. Page 19.

New South Wales Minerals Council chairman and Coal & Allied Ltd managing director Terry O'Reilly yesterday released the results of the Minerals Council/Coopers & Lybrand financial survey, which found that Australia's coal producers are facing their toughest year in ten because of the high exchange rate and lower coal prices to Japan. Page 20
THE AUSTRALIAN

Economists argued yesterday that the figures from the Federal Government's first mid-year review of the Budget left the door open for a further interest rate cut. The share market yesterday staged a modest rally after the release of the Budget review, after being battered by another Wall Street fall. Page 31.

In a further shake-up of Australia's casino industry, Crown Ltd announced it had begun negotiations to purchase the management contracts for the Melbourne casino from Lloyd Williams' Hudson Conway Ltd. Kerry Packer, the recent buyer of 85 per cent of Sydey Harbour Casino Ltd, is a substantial shareholder in both Hudson Conway and Crown. Page 31.

As the Seven Network continues its legal pressure on fellow Optus Vision shareholders, Optus Communications warned that if Seven is successful with its claim, it could acquire Optus Communications' 46.5 per cent stake in Optus Vision at about "half the subscription price". Page 31.

Reef Casino Trust Ltd, the owner of the Reef Casino in Cairns, is being closely monitored by the Australian Securities Commission because it has consistently missed its prospectus forecasts by a large margin. Reef announced on Friday its December quarter revenues fell by more than a third short of Budget despite losses pared to A$2.88 million. Page 33.

Bank of Melbourne chief executive David Airey has been hired by the ANZ Bank to become the managing director of the Bank's New Zealand operations. Airey will leave Bank of Melbourne - well regarded as the best-run regional bank in Australia in recent yeas - at a crucial time, with the Wallis inquiry scheduled to review banking industry takeover regulations. Page 33.

Telecasters North Queensland Ltd directors are confident the proposal to become a pure investment vehicle for the Ten Group Ltd will go to shareholders next month, despite falling behind schedule. TNQ holds a 20 per cent economic and 40 per cent voting interest in Ten. Page 33.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In an attempt to restore profit growth and address sharemarket concerns about its strategic direction, CSR is looking to raise over A$1 billion from a shake-up of its Australian timber operations and United States construction material business. CSR may Also get rid of its underperforming businesses and reinvest some of the proceeds in operations that offer higher growth potential. Page 25.

In a plan to increase its cash flow to A$77 million - a move which would signal a raise in revenue of A$200 million since Christmas - Crown Ltd is looking to buy the Crown Casino management contract from Hudson Conway. Crown will seek shareholder approva to allow Hudson Conway to exercise an option to buy 74.5 million Crown shares at an exercise price of A$1.03 a share. Page 25.

Following lower scrap metal prices and a slow demand for steel products, scrap metals trader Simsmetal has slashed interim dividend by a third to 14 cents a share. Net profits have been cut by 43 per cent - A$14.07 million to December 31 compared with A$4.64 million for the previous corresponding period. Page 27.

The Downing Centre local court was told yesterday the Aust-Wide Property Trust, facing Australian Securities Commission proceedings, was facing an unsustainable daily net funds outflow of A$920,000 around July 1990, the time the management company resolve to freeze the redemption of units. Page 27.

Listed property developer Ipoh and the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation (GIC) may look at forming a listed property trust that could include the newly acquired 175 Liverpool Street office block and the famous A$240 million Queen Victoria Building in Sydney. Page 27.

New South Wales Minerals Council chairman Terry O'Reilly yesterday outlined a tough time ahead for the State's coal industry because of increased competition domestically, a poor exchange rate, and the refusal of the industry's Japanese customers to offerbetter prices. Page 29.
THE AGE

In a surprise development, Crown Casino has confirmed it is holding talks with Hudson Conway over the possible purchase of the casino management contract. The purchase, believed to return around A$300 to A$400 million to HudCon, would see HudCon exercisig A$76.77 million of options over Crown shares more than two years ahead of schedule and at a 10 per cent discount. Page C1.

Bank of Melbourne chief executive David Airey will take over as managing director of the ANZ Bank's New Zealand operations, a move that makes him a candidate to succeed ANZ's current CEO Don Mercer. However, the move leaves Bank of Melbourne stranded at time when it, as a prime takeover target, could be affected by the recommendations of the Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial system. Page C1.

Great Central Mines was yesterday unable to deliver on its quarterly production forecasts at its Bronzewing gold mine in Western Australia, which it blamed on its contractors, an unavailability of equipment, and the need to develop a new underground resouce at the mine. However, the company said the problems would soon be rectified. Page C2.

The deadline for bids for Australia's airports to the Federal Finance Department close tomorrow. The nine bidding groups, bidding towards A$1.3 billion apiece for Melbourne and Brisbane airports, will attempt to show they can squeeze every last dollar of earnings from their targets. Page C3.

Optus Communications shareholder Mayne Nickless revealed yesterday the Seven Network has stepped up its legal attack on its fellow Optus Vision shareholders by formally claiming the right to buy them out. Mayne revealed a successful court action for Seve could see the network buy Optus Vision for as little as A$650 million. Page C3.

Ashton Mining chief executive John Robinson said yesterday the company's North American diamond interests have uncovered promising rock formations in the undiscovered Canadian province of Alberta. Ashton Mining of Canada, which is working the area and also has interests in the Northwest Territories, is 62 per cent owned by Melbourne-based Ashton Mining. Page C2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
